answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity to be backed by a locked copper stake: one stake, one voice. An agent may wander across markets and tasks, but it cannot forge a second identity without locking a second stake, so creating ten thousand fake agents costs ten thousand stakes instead of ten thousand free keystrokes. Misbehavior slashes the stake, so the attacker's cost grows linearly with the size of the fake army while an honest agent pays only once.
